# Refinement update — November 9, 2026

The existing site is preserved. This update improves exploration, reading and historical presentation. GPU rendering and physical-device touch performance remain unverified in this environment; the checklist is not fully certified.

1. **Historical corrections.** The Marian Psalter is dated to early fifteenth-century development rather than a single invention date. The Pius V source label now matches its English Dominican destination. Exact papal document dates are displayed; Dominican tradition and Fátima private revelation remain qualified. Vatican documents, Dominican sources, Catholic Encyclopedia, Dynamic Catholic and the shrine schedule were compared in the source audit.
2. **Marian Psalter and Lepanto.** The new Psalter illustration shows a simple wooden counting cord with knotted ends and larger separators, not a modern 59-bead rosary. London Museum's fourteenth–fifteenth-century wooden/cotton prayer beads support the material choice; the artwork is representative, not a replica or a claim of exactly 150 beads. Lepanto now shows opposing oared, lateen-rigged galleys, cannon smoke and coherent waterlines. The isolated procedural fleet and separate water plane are removed from the active scene. The battle remains a painted image in a 3D camera journey, not a volumetric naval simulation.
3. **Luminous Mysteries.** The supplied John Paul II paragraph and all five descriptions are used verbatim. Each mystery has its Scripture reference and a Rosarium Virginis Mariae link. The five existing images are retained, enlarged, selectable, and highlighted. Description content occupies the chapter's reading area rather than a popup over the pope.
4. **Cinematic presentation.** Image-edge alpha blending softens rectangular borders without altering original image pixels. The celestial bridge now occupies 38% rather than 50% of each chapter interval. Camera paths remain reversible and maintain tested focal bounds. Prominent reconstruction labels are removed; provenance remains in Sources & Credits. Dates use larger responsive gold typography.
5. **External links.** The final authored-content audit covers 65 unique URLs: 61 direct HTTP200 responses; four USCCB403 responses independently verified through web retrieval as the correct Scripture chapters. No broken destination was identified in that sweep. The former unavailable Ourém coordinate reference was replaced with a verified Fátima chapel reference, and its point updated to39.63166,-8.67332. Detailed tables retain dated results; network status can change.
6. **Earth zoom.** Earth radius is3. Camera minimum distance changes from8 to3.65 after the8K texture loads, or4.2 with4K. Devices unable to load a higher-resolution surface retain a5.2 safety limit. Surface clearance improves from5 to0.65/1.2 world units. NASA native8192×4096 imagery is loaded only for capable larger displays;4096×2048 is used elsewhere. This supports regional geography, not street-level buildings. Mouse wheel, pinch, buttons and keyboard use bounded exponential zoom; markers scale with camera distance.
7. **Globe usability.** Separate Browse Locations and Location Details states replace the competing list/detail layout. Added Back, Previous/Next, Focus on Location, Reset Earth View and expandable/collapsible reading controls. Selection survives manual rotation and reset. Mobile uses a bottom sheet with swipe handling on its header. Panel scrolling remains separate from globe zoom and timeline travel. All9 historical locations and32 shrine schedule entries remain. Each shrine has individualized sourced context and a prominent intention. Licensed photographs added for St Peter's and Fátima with linked credits.
8. **Testing.** Node checks pass for59 beads,53 Hail Mary/6 Our Father beads,20 mysteries,75 prayer steps across22 stages, all shrine markers, hemisphere selection, dataset isolation, camera continuity and focal bounds at1440×900,768×1024,390×844 and844×390. Browser checks covered desktop map modes, search, selection, focus/reset retention, and mobile portrait/landscape reading, expansion/collapse and Cana selection. Browser WebGL is disabled: actual shader compilation, rendered close Earth quality, camera appearance, pinch on physical touch hardware and frame rate still require a capable device. The earlier recording and supplied/generated asset images were visually inspected.
9. **Final invitation.** The unchanged Sky Surfer Immersive Rosary link has a stronger antique-gold halo on a four-second cycle, clear hover/focus styling and a static reduced-motion presentation.
10. **Limits.** The2D sacred artwork and new battle remain artistic interpretations. Two shrine destinations have new documentary photos; others retain appropriate existing art or text. Shrine context varies in depth according to available evidence. Higher-resolution Earth textures increase GPU memory use, so the4K fallback is retained. No claim is made that every mandatory visual/device test has passed.

See SOURCE-AUDIT-7.md, SOURCE-AUDIT-7-ADDENDUM.md, ASSET-MANIFEST.md and photo-metadata-7.json in the source package for evidence and licenses.
